title: Photometric mesh refinement without depth maps (photo_refine), 2026-10-13
inputs: YCB power drill and mustard bottle, 300 DSLR photos each from five heights, own masks and own recovered cameras; scans only for scoring, each mesh with its own ICP similarity fit (a few hundredths at 0.5 % are within the fit).
method: anchor vertices search along the smoothed mesh normal; 5x5 patch on the tangent plane, 1.2 reduced pixels apart in the reference view; reference = most frontal view that sees the vertex (point z-buffer of the mesh), up to five views 8-35 degrees away; score = mean normalised cross-correlation with the reference patch; acceptance: score >= 0.55, >= photo_refine_peak (0.15) above the median over 17 offsets, >= 0.08 above staying, not at the end of the range; offsets spread by 200 averaging steps weighted by score; inward only when the silhouette comes first; two Taubin cycles per round; rounds of 6, 3, 1.5 edge lengths
cost: search 3 s per round on 300 views (Apple M1, 4 threads); reading 300 photos of 4272x2848 again 70-90 s; peak resident 5.8-6.8 GB in the whole run
defaults: photo_refine=2 applies only when the silhouette comes first (cameras at several heights); Bunny and Lucy fusion-only meshes byte-identical to before
checks: 217 library tests (an inflated sphere mesh is pulled onto the photographed sphere; welding), rustfmt, clippy native with and without capi, threaded WebAssembly build
limits: Two objects. Fine relief is still missing. The mustard bottle gains nothing and loses 0.03 at 0.5 % within the fit. Not run in a browser; the photos are read a second time. Forced on for single-turn captures it has not passed the six-object gate. No third-party code; not patent clearance.

single_turn_forced_on.note: six 3DLF objects, fusion from their own default depths, photo_refine=1 (both directions)

reference_methods_same_captures.data: crops at half size (drill 544x576, mustard 432x704), 300 views, our masks and cameras; Tesla T4
reference_methods_same_captures.reading: scores close to ours; rendered, the neural surface shows relief (vents, chuck ridges, seams) that ours lacks; printed labels become shallow relief; undersides rough
